title: Cultural (In)Competence: Investigating Culture-Specific Stereotype Detection Capabilities of LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.22545v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Stereotypes are subjective constructs that are mediated by the cultural context in which they are viewed. Successfully modeling them thus also requires cultural competence. When using large language models (LLMs) for stereotype-related tasks, such as their detection, it is therefore crucial that models can access relevant cultural knowledge and adjust responses accordingly. Since LLMs have shown disparities in what cultural knowledge is available to them, their capacity regarding stereotypes may also be disparate across languages and cultural contexts (e.g., for non-English languages or for non-US contexts). In this paper, we systematically investigate the effectiveness of LLMs for culture-specific stereotype detection across three factors: (1) the prompting language, (2) the instruction tuning language, and (3) the fine-tuning dataset size. translated_abstract: 刻板印象是由其所处的文化语境所调节的主观建构，因此，要成功地对其进行建模，同样需要文化胜任力。当使用大语言模型（LLM）执行与刻板印象相关的任务（如刻板印象检测）时，模型能够获取相关文化知识并据此调整响应至关重要。由于大语言模型在可获取的文化知识方面存在差异，它们在不同语言和文化语境下（例如非英语语言或非美国语境）处理刻板印象的能力也可能存在差异。本文系统性地研究了三个因素对大语言模型进行文化特定刻板印象检测效果的影响：（1）提示语言；（2）指令微调语言；（3）微调数据集规模。我们针对美国、荷兰和中国文化语境开展了实验。我们的结果表明，大语言模型……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文系统研究了提示语言、指令微调语言和微调数据集规模这三个因素对大语言模型在美国、荷兰和中国等不同文化语境下检测文化特定刻板印象能力的影响，揭示了模型文化胜任力方面的差异。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically investigates how the prompting language, instruction tuning language, and fine-tuning dataset size affect LLMs' culture-specific stereotype detection capabilities across US, Dutch, and Chinese cultural contexts, revealing disparities in their cultural competence.
